quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What do large trucks do when turning onto a street with two lanes in each direction?

options.text: They can turn into either of the two lanes.
They often need to use the left lane to complete the turn.
They must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: They often need to use the left lane to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: Large trucks must swing wide to complete a right turn. The truck may look like it is turning left because it swings so wide. Watch the truck's turn signal to know which way it is really turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: What is the speed limit at an uncontrolled railroad crossing?

options.text: 25 mph.
15 mph.
20 mph.

questions.explanation: When you are within 100 feet of an uncontrolled railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions, you must drive 15 mph or slower.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with stop signs on all four corners at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You do.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn.

questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle parallel to the curb on a level street, what is required?

options.text: Your front wheels must be turned toward the street.
Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
One of your rear wheels must touch the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking next to the curb on a level street, your front and back wheels must be parallel to the curb and within 18 inches of it.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into the first lane.
Turn into the second lane.

questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs and message boards warn you of workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions immediately ahead. This sign warns about an upcoming right curve.

questions.question: Blocking an intersection during rush hour traffic is not permitted:

options.text: Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
Under any circumstances, even if your light is green.
Unless you have the right-of-way or a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances, even if your light is green.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross before the light turns red, even if your light is green. You can get a ticket for blocking the intersection.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when it is necessary to avoid collisions. Do not use your horn to tell a driver to go faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and keep your current speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to avoid staying in the oncoming lane. Return to your previous lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.explanation: Keep at least a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly, and following too closely is dangerous. If the motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid the rider. The risk of falling is higher on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does this mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians may use a white cane or guide dog. You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is not working, you must:

options.text: Stop, then proceed when safe.
Stop before entering the intersection and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop only if necessary.

questions.explanation: If a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as if stop signs are in all directions. Stop and proceed carefully when it is safe.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.
questions.explanation: Never try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you make your turn.

questions.question: Safely backing your vehicle requires all of the following, except:

options.text: Looking over your right shoulder as you back up.
Checking your vehicle's surroundings.
Tapping your horn before you back up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tapping your horn before you back up.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because it is hard to see behind your vehicle. Before you get in, check the area around your vehicle for hazards. When backing out of a parking space, look over your shoulder to see your surroundings.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When can you transport animals in the back of a pickup truck?

options.text: The truck bed sides are at least 18 inches high.
The animals are properly secured.
The tailgate is closed.

questions.explanation: Animals in the back of a truck must be properly secured. This prevents them from falling, jumping, or being thrown out of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which roadway freezes first when wet?

options.text: Bridges and overpasses
Intersections
Tunnels

questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other roads.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The far left lane.
The center lane.

questions.explanation: Start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a car?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the car you just passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to move back.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. They often make sudden changes in direction. Remember that children and bicycles are small and can be hard to see.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross.
Go around them to the right.

questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb (or uphill with no curb), turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn toward the center so the car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: What does slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events cause?

options.text: Traffic congestion.
Fewer rear-end collisions.
Better traffic flow.

questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual events. This "rubbernecking" causes traffic jams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves or gets narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves or gets narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road direction is changing or the road is narrowing. You may see these signs on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear in blind spots or are too close for the driver to stop or steer safely.
Areas where cars have enough space behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear in blind spots or are too close for the driver to stop or steer safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear in blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or steer safely. Staying in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop completely.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, be ready for sudden changes. Watch for signals from other drivers. Expect cars merging at on-ramps and be prepared for quick changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What is a distraction when driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve.
Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: What can happen if you abandon an animal on the highway?

options.text: You can go to jail.
Points are added against your license.
No legal consequences.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to dump or abandon an animal on the highway. Punishment can include up to six months in jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way just because the rules say you do. Always consider the situation at an intersection. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.
